summary: William R. LaFleur worked in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies after studying at the University of Chicago (~1968-1973). He held posts at Princeton University (~1971-1978), UCLA (~1978-1989), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1989-2010).

William Rainey Harper was a linguistics and religious studies scholar who studied at Yale under William Dwight Whitney (~1873-1875). He held posts at Denison University (~1876-1879) and the University of Chicago (~1891-1906).
William Robertson was an indology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Edinburgh from ~1733 to 1741 and later held a post there from ~1762 to 1793.
William Roxburgh studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1770-1772) and the University of Aberdeen (~1790). In 1793, he served as director at the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

William S.-Y. Wang studied at Columbia University (~1951-1955) and the University of Michigan (~1955-1960). A scholar of linguistics and sinology, he held posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1966-1994) and Hong Kong Polytechnic University (~2015).
William Stede worked in indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at SOAS University of London and the University of London from ~1928 to 1949.

William Theodore de Bary was a scholar of sinology, Japanology, and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (1937-1941, 1947-1953) and Harvard University (~1941-1942), later serving as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia (~1953-1990).

William Van Gordon, a Buddhist and religious studies scholar, founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and was attested in 2015 as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University.

William Wilson Hunter studied at The Glasgow Academy, the University of Glasgow (~1855-1860), the University of Paris (~1860-1861), and the University of Bonn (~1861-1862). In indology and history, he worked in the Indian Civil Service (~1862-1887) and Calcutta University (~1886-1887).
William Woodville Rockhill was a scholar in tibetology and sinology. He completed his studies at Lycée Condorcet (~1868-1871) and the École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871-1873).

William Wright was a linguistics and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of St Andrews (~1845-1849). He held positions at University College London (~1855-1856), the British Museum (~1861-1870), and the University of Cambridge (~1870-1889).

Willibald Kirfel, an indology scholar, studied at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi (~1904-1908), whom he later succeeded. In 1920, he held a post at the University of Bonn as librarian and Privatdozent.

Wilt L. Idema is a sinologist who studied at Leiden University (~1963-1974) under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (~1965-1974). He held posts as professor at Leiden (1975-1999), fellow at Radcliffe (2001-2002), and faculty and director at Harvard (~1999-2013).
Winfred Robert Martin was a scholar of indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College and worked as a librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan, a religious studies scholar, studied at Cornell (~1967-1971). She held posts at Washington and Lee University (~1994-2000), the University of Chicago (~2000-2005), and Indiana University (~2012).
Winston Kyan works in history, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung (attested 2006).

Wolfgang Morgenroth worked in indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild (~1950-1958) and held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1976-1992) and the University of Potsdam (2020).

Wolfram Eberhard studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1927-1933) and worked in sinology and history. He held posts at Ankara University (~1937-1948) and as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1948-1976).
Woncheol Yun is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Stony Brook University. He was attested in 2012 as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University.

Woosung Huh works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hawaii and was attested in 2012 as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University.
